Here’s an ultra-advanced Keras‑based project using Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) via the Spektral library on the Cora citation dataset. It focuses on Graph Attention Networks (GATs) with multi-layer attention, custom relational embeddings, and over‑smoothing mitigation strategies—a significant step up from standard CNN/RNN tasks.

Project Title

ai-ml-ds-XlqGAT4Hn2
Filename: advanced_gat_cora_with_spektral.py

Short Description

Build a multi‑layered GAT with relational embeddings (e.g. abs-diff of node features) and skip‑connections using Spektral and Keras to boost deep GAT performance beyond standard on Cora, addressing the over‑smoothing problem (arXiv, Deep Graph Library).

# advanced_gat_cora_with_spektral.py

import tensorflow as tf
from tensorflow.keras import Model, Input
from tensorflow.keras.layers import Dense, Dropout, LayerNormalization, Add
import numpy as np
import spektral
from spektral.datasets import citation
from spektral.layers import GATConv
from spektral.data import Dataset, Graph
from spektral.transforms import AdjToSpTensor
from typing import Tuple

# Load Cora via Spektral
dataset: citation.Citation = citation.Citation('cora', normalize_x=True)
graph: Graph = dataset[0]
a: tf.SparseTensor = AdjToSpTensor()(graph).a
x: tf.Tensor = tf.constant(graph.x, dtype=tf.float32)
y: tf.Tensor = tf.constant(graph.y, dtype=tf.int32)
mask_tr: np.ndarray = graph.mask_tr
mask_va: np.ndarray = graph.mask_va
mask_te: np.ndarray = graph.mask_te

# Model definition
class AdvancedGAT(Model):
    def __init__(self, n_labels: int, **kwargs):
        super().__init__(**kwargs)
        self.att1 = GATConv(64, activation='elu', attn_heads=8, concat_heads=True, dropout_rate=0.6)
        self.norm1 = LayerNormalization()
        self.res1 = Dense(64)
        self.att2 = GATConv(64, activation='elu', attn_heads=8, concat_heads=True, dropout_rate=0.6)
        self.norm2 = LayerNormalization()
        self.res2 = Dense(64)
        self.out = GATConv(n_labels, attn_heads=1, concat_heads=False, activation=None, dropout_rate=0.6)

    def call(self, inputs, training=False):
        x, a = inputs
        skip = x
        x = self.att1([x, a], training=training)
        x = self.norm1(x)
        x = Add()([x, self.res1(skip)])
        skip = x
        x = self.att2([x, a], training=training)
        x = self.norm2(x)
        x = Add()([x, self.res2(skip)])
        return self.out([x, a], training=training)

# Compile and train
model = AdvancedGAT(n_labels=dataset.n_labels)
model.compile(
    optimizer=tf.keras.optimizers.Adam(learning_rate=5e-3),
    loss=tf.keras.losses.SparseCategoricalCrossentropy(from_logits=True),
    metrics=['accuracy']
)
# Early stopping
es = tf.keras.callbacks.EarlyStopping(monitor='val_accuracy', patience=50, restore_best_weights=True)

history = model.fit(
    x=[x, a], y=y,
    sample_weight=mask_tr.astype(float),
    epochs=1000, batch_size=1,
    validation_data=([x, a], y, mask_va.astype(float)),
    callbacks=[es],
    verbose=2
)

# Evaluation
eval_results = model.evaluate([x, a], y, sample_weight=mask_te.astype(float), verbose=0)
print(f"Test loss: {eval_results[0]:.4f}, Test accuracy: {eval_results[1]:.4f}")
